This game was pretty fun.
You start out small, just getting a fresh version of Hacknet's OS from someone named "Bit". Bit is now dead, and it's up to you to find out what caused their death. You go from some simple script kiddie porthacking vulnerable machines and gathering programs to changing IP addresses, popping servers down like it's nothing, deleting system files and bricking machines like it's going out of style. You go from a kid with a legoset to a demon with a supercomputer filled with all sorts of port-cracking programs.

+Learning Curve is perfect.
+Lots to read if you don't mind a bit of work
+Getting extra port-opening programs is extremely fun, especially finding the hard-to-get ones ;)
+You feel like a baller hacker by the end of the game
+Finding programs feels awesome, you earned these port-crackers kiddo
+Forkbombing people after wiping their drive never gets old
+Hacking honeypots without your x-sys is a nice challenge. Only dweebs need a GUI.
+S O U N D T R A C K
+Tracekill.exe

+/-Only one active tracer in the game, unlocks /el though...
+/-Why does notes.exe take up so much RAM??!?!?!
+/-No option to post on /el

-Deleting logs does nearly nothing, and is needed for only one specific part of the game. (Two if you count Academic logs but I never tried that.) It feels like leaving a trail of IPs isn't really that big of a deal because local sysadmins do not care about back-tracing you and deleting you off the map like they should.
-Some missions are convoluted near the end, requiring very specific triggers to get to the next part of the ending mission.
-There is no cause/effect system in the game. This is the worst offender. I feel as if I should be punished for bringing down a major international email server, a major OS development website/server, two security software companies, and /el in under 10 minutes. I at least feel as if picking a fight with /el would be like picking a fight with a group of senior football players in high school as a freshman.
-No achievement for beating the game in terminal-only mode, the ability to play with nothing but a pad and pen listing the J-mail IP address, the terminal, and "help".
-Changing IP is too easy, there needs to be additional layers of security every time you break in.
-No way to access Proxy busters from Terminal view.
-Forkbombing someone without any of their server files should wipe them from the map permanently.

I strongly reccomend Hacknet for anyone who has even a slight interest in computer science. The game is essentially one big puzzle in which you, a new member to an evolving hacker community are thrust into. The game draws you in and although somtimes repepative is consistantly adding new ways intrigue the player. Hacknet is masterfully crafted and is worth your money.

To be fair Uplink is better. This game is good because you get to use the keyboard. Uplink is a hacking game where keyboard is not used, so the biggest flaw is now solved. Problem is the game lacks a bit of adrenaline. 

1) Most servers don't trace you, so you can just hang around forever.
2) Its not clear where you are connected too. Once you hack a place is there opened forever. You don't even have to disconnect.
3) You clear your logs but not the disconnected log, which makes no sense. In Uplink you have to clear logs at origin and destination, seems more realistic.
4) Its too easy to go up the ranking. 
5) In Uplink you had money to worry about. Upgrade hardware and buy software. In Hacknet all you get is reputation, that also have no impact besides gettings invitations.
6) The game does not allow you to accept more than 1 mission.
7) The storyline is a bit broken. I made 1 mission that lead to a hacker invading my computer, that leads to another mission and to another mission and basically you cannot accept other mission while the "story" is leading you in 1 way. That made me join an organization and now I cannot finish the old missions. Basically I lost 3 missions, cannot be played.
8) The game UI is a bit limited. I cannot open a file and an email at the same time. Which makes very annoying to take note to things. Althought I cannot complain much on that, as in Uplink I really had a pen and paper next to me all the time, in this game I never used real paper so far.
9) Uplink allow you to do other stuff, such as Stock Market, browse any server, etc. Hacknet is limited. You only get the servers IP when the game wants you to get. There is not freedom besides follow the story.
10) Uplink allows you to choose which mission to make, in the sense of choosing to be a good or a bad hacker. In Hacknet some missions presentation don't have more than 2 lines. You have to accept missions without even knowing what skills you need, what tools you need and what you have to do. Its really 1 path only. And if you try to get missions in different orders you lose them, just like I lost 3. UPDATE: Because of this 1 path only + cannot accept more than 1 mission, you can game over all the time. If you delete the wrong file, edit the wrong record, its finished. People call this bug in the forum, I call this lack of flexibility. In Uplink you could simply give up on a mission and pay a fine. If you delete a file you are suppose to upload, it shouldn't be game over, just some kind of punishment.
11) It uses Unix commands but limit them. For instance you have rm command but cannot be used to delete folders. Cannot download folders either.
12) Find it a bit weird that no special software is required to know when you are being traced.
13) So far the challenge of the game seems to be more about curiosity of the player. Meaning you have to look into every folder and file and read and see what you can find (be aware) rather than having a challenge on the hacking it self, such as limited time, required software, go throught LAN networks, etc.
14) You can hack a webserver, a main frame, a home pc or a cell phone, they all look the same, they all have same file structure, they are all hacked with same tools. A bit boring no?
15) Network map completely unecessary. Its just a harder way to find servers, if you are not going to use it to bounce like Uplink, why have that? Just a window with animated blue balls. A list with a search box and some favorites would do the job, or better, connect always using the line command, IP or name assigned by the user.
16) Once you scan a server and it reveals other computers connected to that, more "balls" appears and its a mystery why some are very distant and some are very close. The distance is based on what? It simple confuses the player as it adds a connection between them and with time the connections cross each other. Well, still trying to figure out why did it this way.
17) I'm already playing this game for hours and all I do is execute programs to open ports.


The good:

a) Very well done interface in the sense that keyboard and mouse usage is well integrated. The key here is keyboard. Its very nice to be able to play the entire game using keyboard only.
b) I like the fact that webserver have website with real images. Just because its a hacker game, it doesn't mean the "normal" internet doesn't exist. Although limited, I liked the www.cfc.com.
c) You can see an effort to bring interesting content to see around. Most servers have files that are not crucial to the missions, things you can read, chats, funny stuff. That really adds to the game and was one of the things I feel lacking in Uplink. Perhaps this is one of the reason a lot of servers don't have tracing mechanism, so you don't have time pressure all the time.
d) Not having time pressure all the time is good, but also removed money pressure and other stuff, which is left it a bit unbalanced.
e) Nice animations. The screens change a lot. Its not the same interface all the time.

Absolutely awesome little hacking game. The aesthetic is really solid, hitting that sort of 'near-future/near-past' UI space that most hacking games strive for. If you've ever worked in a *NIX environment, you'll feel right at home. The music is another spot where this game really nails it, has this really gritty cyberpunk feel to it. Also features one of my favorite Carpenter Brut tracks, Roller Mobster.

As for gameplay, it's pretty straightforward. You're sent an email from a dead hacker's failsafe asking you to look into his death. You work your way into various hacker organizations, acquire new tools, and push the story forward. The early missions tend toward the trivial if you've ever worked in a *NIX environment, but once you get into the later missions, putting together the pieces becomes more important than just breaking into servers and rummaging around.

If I had to compare it to anything, I'd say it reminded me quite a bit of Uplink: Hacker Elite and Digital: A Love Story. Uplink is the obvious comparison and HackNet takes a lot of queues from how Uplink's story was told and presented to the player. Digital does a lot of this, too, with the way players have to use the things they find to dig up more clues. I'd say HackNet's story is more similar to Digital in how it sets and escalates stakes, overall. So if you like either or both of those? This is a no-brainer.

I've been a huge fan of the "hacker game" ever since I first played 1985's [i]Hacker[/i] on my Amstrad CPC: I'm pretty hardened to the genre, and I can confidently say that not since [i]Uplink[/i] has anything broken through my firewall like [i][b]Hacknet[/b][/i] did. If you're looking for an easy-to-pick up and compelling puzzle game in a cyberpunk theme, it's a clear winner: I got 6 hours of thoroughly enjoyable playtime out of it, and I'm sure I'll go back and get the same again when I find the chance to go and explore deeper.

Very creative with great visuals and an intuitive interface (for anyone who's ever played around in the Unix shell you'll be right at home). Even with no experience the game seems pretty easy to pick up. It has a very interesting story, although it's all text based so if you're not interested in reading... that's going to be a big downside.

The only thing I didn't like was how short it was. I was able to beat the game in about 6-7 hours... and while it was challenging it left me wanting more. With that said, the creator does send you an email (in-game) that reveals some things that will make another play through worthwhile.

Highly recommend for anyone interested in "hacking" or simply a different take on things.

It takes all the things I loved about Introversion's Uplink, and gets rid of the main issue I had with it. The routing through bundles of servers and having to remove your logs from each and every single server, each and every single time. So tedious it's unbelievable. You still have to remove logs in Hacknet, but thankfully it's a lot more straightforward. This game keeps all the fun parts, the espionage and the feeling of curiosity. There's plenty to read on all the servers, even a lot of flavour text not even related to the game.

Honestly, this is one of the best hacker games I've played, and if my profile is anything to go by, I own most of them available on Steam. It's nowhere near as unforgiving as Hacker Evolution, and nowhere near as tedious as Uplink can get in it's mid to late game.

I can't say too much more without going into spoiler territory, but there's a point about 30-45 minutes in that makes you go "wow... what on earth do I do now?" - and you need to call on all the skills you've learned so far to get past it. The feeling of accomplishment when it works out is amazing.

These guys better be making this into a series like Hacker Evolution, because it has incredible potential, and I'm loving every second.

Pretty fun hacking sim with a good soundtrack to boot. There aren't any made up protocols or anything like that, and the inclusion of an actual command line was pretty nice. There are alternate paths, which I won't spoil, and the missions vary the formula of open ports run porthack enough to keep you entertained for the duration of the game. If you aren't a fast typer, don't worry; after the tutorial you are able to choose between using the gui or the command line. I'd reccomend it if you like computers, hacking sims, or want to look cool in front of your friends.
